findings.element: SURFACE / VERDICT — Comfort design (Comfort Home, seam door, Comfort Now, Talk to someone, steady card, AI safety card). FOR: a congregant in crisis on a phone, often late, often offline-ish; plus a pastor texting a link.
findings.ruling: VERDICT: FIX FIRST (11). The subtraction work is right and should ship: killing the duplicate chapter, pairing verse to chapter, removing the count/grade/quota, keeping the door out of the path sheet and off a sixth tab, and holding the whole thing behind a deploy preview. The defects are all in the new safety plumbing, where a wrong answer is worse than no feature.
findings.change: Ship steps 1-3 (instrumentation, one-entry content, kill the duplicate) as one preview PR; hold the crisis-line and pastoral-request work until findings 1-4 and 7 are closed.

findings.element: Crisis-line region resolver, timezone tier — /Users/ashleymarkevans/futures-daily-word/src/utils/geo.ts:26-31 `campusFromTimezone` maps every `America/*` timezone to 'US'
findings.ruling: Never show the wrong country's number — the design's own worst-case failure. Reusing or mirroring this helper shows 988 to a reader in Rio (America/Sao_Paulo), Bogota or Mexico City the moment IP fails or they are offline; Futures has a Brazilian campus.
findings.change: Write an independent tz->country allowlist in src/utils/crisis-lines.ts (explicit prefixes per supported line only) returning `unknown` for anything unlisted, and add a test asserting no input path ever returns 988; never call campusFromTimezone from the crisis resolver.

findings.element: Region cache — /Users/ashleymarkevans/futures-daily-word/src/utils/geo.ts:47-57 `detectCountry()` caches the country in sessionStorage
findings.ruling: The design promises the crisis line renders offline, always, from local data. sessionStorage dies with the tab, so a cold offline open — the exact 2am case — resolves to unknown and shows no number.
findings.change: On every successful resolve, persist `{region, source, line}` to localStorage under dw_crisis_region and paint the card from that on mount before any network call.

findings.element: Resolver precedence 'campus beats everything' vs CAMPUSES — /Users/ashleymarkevans/futures-daily-word/src/data/tokens.ts:79 `{ id: 'other', name: 'Non-Futures Church', region: 'Other' }`
findings.ruling: A saved campus of 'Non-Futures Church' (or any region the lines file has no entry for) terminates resolution, so a reader in Atlanta who picked it sees no number when IP would have given 988. Duty of care lost to a data value, silently.
findings.change: Treat region 'Other'/absent/unmapped as unresolved and fall through campus -> IP -> timezone; only a total absence of signal shows the local-emergency sentence and the directory link.

findings.element: ?comfort=1 cold-device door vs the app's other overlays — /Users/ashleymarkevans/futures-daily-word/src/App.tsx:498 `{!needsPushOnboarding && !showPathAsk && <CookieConsent />}`, :480 EmailGate, :236-239 Day1Landing, PWAInstall
findings.ruling: The design only excludes saveSetup, Door 3 and push. The link a pastor texts to a hospital car park therefore opens on a cold device with a cookie banner, and can pick up the install prompt and Day 1 landing, on top of the verse. 'Nothing is asked of you here' is then false on the first paint.
findings.change: Add COMFORT_DEEP_LINK beside SERMON_DEEP_LINK at App.tsx:35 and gate CookieConsent, EmailGate, PWAInstall, EmailNudge and Day1Landing off it exactly as the sermon deep link already does.

findings.element: Self-serve levers — public/comfort/care.json and public/comfort/lines.json described as 'a campus pastor edits a JSON file'
findings.ruling: Self-serve over developer levers: a file in public/ needs a git commit, a build and a deploy — that is Ashley, not a pastor, and a crisis number or a care pastor changing is exactly the hard-week edit that must not queue behind him. The design's own honest-exception paragraph does not cover these two.
findings.change: Keep content.json and flags.json as repo assets, but move the per-campus care recipient and the per-region crisis line into the existing `campus_content` Supabase table served by netlify/functions/campus-content.js, so a change is a row edit with the JSON as bundled fallback.

findings.element: Seam comfort door — /Users/ashleymarkevans/futures-daily-word/src/index.css:824-836 `.dw-seam-bar { height: calc(34px + var(--safe-top)) }`, `.dw-seam-link { font-size: 11px }`, and :876-881 `:root .dw-seam-bar a.dw-seam-link { color: var(--dw-gold) !important }`
findings.ruling: Mobile first, tap targets: the one tap that must never miss would be an ~11px label in a 34px strip, third item at 375px between the wordmark, 'Daily Word' and 'Futures Church ↗'. And the !important rule repaints any new anchor gold, not the muted weight the design specifies — two accents in the chrome.
findings.change: Render it as `<button class="dw-cmf-seam">` (escapes the .dw-seam-link rule) with a 44px min hit area overflowing the strip, and hide the 'Daily Word' word below 390px so three items fit without wrapping.

findings.element: 'Talk to a pastor' CTA — shipped in build step 5 while the route that delivers it (step 9, pastoral_requests) is held dark pending the named-recipient decision
findings.ruling: Duty of care created and not met, which the design names as its top risk, and a control that does nothing on a crisis screen. Also: never point a person at a control that cannot act.
findings.change: Until a named recipient exists per campus, the button does not render at all — the card ships as crisis line + campus phone + one honest sentence; no greyed or dead CTA.

findings.element: Pastoral request form — 'Failed: That didn't send' copy with no stated placement, and no empty-field handling
findings.ruling: Errors render where the eye is, beside the button pressed; noValidate plus an explicit required check, because iOS native validation is silent. A crisis message that silently fails validation is the worst version of this bug.
findings.change: Set noValidate on the form; an empty textarea on Send renders one line directly under Send ('Write a line or two first'), and the send-failure line renders in that same spot with the crisis number beneath it.

findings.element: Return-day check-in copy ('Still here. Want the same passage, or a new one?') and the AI quick prompt 'Why does this hurt so much'
findings.ruling: Internal contradiction with the path's printed, unchangeable promise 'Comfort scriptures. Nothing else asked of you' and with the design's own presence-before-explanation principle (Pargament). A two-button question is an ask; a prompt that requests a reason invites the explanation the design excludes Romans 8:28 for.
findings.change: Make the check-in a single plain link, 'Read a different passage', and replace the first quick prompt with a presence one ('Say the thing you can't say out loud'); keep 'Read me something for tonight'.

findings.ruling: The change list says move the indigo values to tokens, which yields clay-tinted gradients. No decorative gradients; quiet, generous, one accent — and low stimulus is the whole point of this screen.
findings.change: Flat `--dw-surface` panels on `--dw-canvas` with a 1px `--dw-border`; no gradient anywhere on a comfort surface, and add the gradient string to the step-3 grep check alongside the indigo hexes.

findings.element: Book cards in the comfort done state ('When you're ready, there's more here')
findings.ruling: Listed as an open decision; it is the only remaining ask on a path that promises none, and it is a sales surface on a crisis screen. Nothing counts, nothing is asked.
findings.change: Cut book cards from comfort entirely rather than moving them into the done state; leave the done line as the last thing on the screen.

findings.ruling: One passage instead of two (the hero fallback at HomeScreen.tsx:1302-1305 as the only chapter surface, ComfortSection reduced to the after-reading frame) is the single biggest user win and is correctly diagnosed. Removing 'Reading x of y', 'You're doing great' and the ask_lock quota (ComfortSection.tsx:96, :300-303, :297-356) honours the printed promise. Pairing verse to chapter, keeping the date-keyed localDayIndex, keeping the streak recorded but invisible, no push, no graduation, no sixth tab, no sixth path card, useSubView alone with a live open prop, and the whole thing behind a deploy preview Ashley approves.
findings.change: Keep as designed; do not let the safety-plumbing fixes delay the duplicate-chapter removal — it can ship as its own preview PR.
